headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Airbyte can move business data broadly while Chatwoot handles customer data and integrations, creating default-path exposure and unverified downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, Airbyte can move data through APIs and Chatwoot consumes messages and integrations; if operators bridge them via files or copied content, malicious text could propagate. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not evidenced as default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-exported text into Chatwoot workflows or integrations
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted payloads into Chatwoot macros
Add a manual review step before any Airbyte output is reused
Use content sanitization for fields that may contain instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and messages. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can move sensitive records across systems through integrations, so leakage is plausible in default enterprise use. Uncertainty about exact storage boundaries pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Airbyte syncs business records that include customer identifiers into Chatwoot-connected systems
IF Chatwoot integrations export conversation content to third-party services
mitigations: Restrict synced fields to minimum necessary
Mask or tokenize identifiers before transfer
Review integration destinations and disable unnecessary exports
Separate credentials and access scopes per system

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git, or shared mutable-resource access. The main overlap is outbound connectivity, which can create coordination issues only if operators point both at the same external API or dataset. That is possible but not default from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or database
IF an orchestrator gives them overlapping mutable credentials
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Document ownership of each external resource
Avoid concurrent writes to the same endpoint
Add locking or queueing around shared destinations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data that Chatwoot may ingest through integrations or operator workflows. Chatwoot's support workflows can then act on that input, so A's output can become B's input without a documented verification step. That creates a realistic cascade from data transformation errors into customer-facing mistakes.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is routed into Chatwoot automations or agent workflows
IF Chatwoot treats imported records as authoritative without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Chatwoot consumes Airbyte output
Sample-check transformed records for schema and semantic errors
Mark imported fields as untrusted in support workflows
Require human approval for customer-facing actions based on imported data

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data while Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and messages. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, but the data classes imply compliance-sensitive processing and possible retention or export mismatches when the pair is used together. Because the exact policy gap is undocumented, medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is synchronized into Airbyte-managed destinations
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Map each data class to an owner and retention rule
Disable exports of regulated fields unless required
Verify deletion and export workflows in both systems
Record the legal basis for each integration
